convention: Regular octahedron. Each of the 8 triangular faces carries one engraved digit, identified via connected-component clustering (weld-by-position + BFS-by-triangle) on the Antique_Gold_UV_PBR material (D8_primitive1, 4573 verts), separated from the die body (Dice_Recess_BlackRed_UV_PBR, D8_primitive0, 24 verts). Each face yields one large glyph component (255-538 verts) plus a small decorative corner-stud component (48-56 verts, not a digit) that clusters into the same face-normal group. IMPORTANT ASSET-SPECIFIC CAVEAT: the glTF root node (__root__) carries a non-identity transform (rotationQuaternion [0,1,0,0] = 180 deg around Y, plus scaling [1,1,-1] = a mirror on Z/X). Reading digits with the camera pointed at RAW LOCAL-SPACE component normals shows the WRONG (mirrored) face. Camera views must use the component's normal transformed by the mesh's full world matrix (computeWorldMatrix(true) + getWorldMatrix()) to land on the correct face; the local normal recorded below is what a runtime consumer reading mesh.getVerticesData(NormalKind) in local/locator space (matching src/dice/procedural.ts convention, same as D6/D4) will see -- it is NOT what you should feed directly to a camera for a human/vision-model screenshot check on this asset.

mesh_notes.D8_primitive0: Dice_Recess_BlackRed_UV_PBR material, 24 vertices -- body/recess trim, not a face.
mesh_notes.D8_primitive1: Antique_Gold_UV_PBR material, 4573 vertices -- body shell (component 0, 1260 verts, centroid at origin) + 8 small corner-stud decorative components (48-56 verts each, one per face, direction proxies only) + 8 large digit-glyph components (255-538 verts each, one per face) -- confirmed by screenshot+vision reading of each of the 8 glyph components independently.

validation_notes: Method: (1) computed connected components on D8_primitive1 via faceDirectionsFromMarkings(0.985), grouping each face's big glyph component with its small corner-stud component by normal similarity -- yielded exactly 8 clusters, one per face, as expected for a regular octahedron. (2) Confirmed geometric structure: cluster normals are the 8 axis-aligned octant directions (+-1,+-1,+-1)/sqrt(3) (dot>=0.998 against the ideal octant vectors), i.e. no meaningful tilt for this asset (unlike D6's documented 'leve tilt'). (3) CRITICAL FIX: discovered the root node has a non-identity world transform (180 deg Y rotation + Z-mirror scale); naively pointing the camera at raw local-space normals (as a prior abandoned attempt in scratch/ appears to have done, per the d8-*.png filenames using m/p octant-sign convention) shows a MIRRORED/wrong face. Re-did all camera shots using normals transformed through mesh.getWorldMatrix() -- verified alignment by projecting each glyph centroid with BABYLON.Vector3.Project and confirming it lands at the exact screen center (320,320 in a 640x640 canvas) for all 8 faces before reading digits. (4) Read each of the 8 faces 3 independently ways: (a) direct ask on cropped+2x-upscaled screenshot, (b) shuffled/relabeled filenames (FACE_ONE..EIGHT, random component order) to rule out sequential-bias in the vision model, (c) detailed stroke-by-stroke description (count straight lines/curves/loops) before final identification, and (d) light-intensity-boosted re-renders for the darker/low-contrast faces (13-16). All 3 independent passes agreed on every face: components 9,10,11,12,13,14,15,16 = digits 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 respectively, with zero contradictions across methods. (5) Geometric opposite-pairing is unambiguous: dot products for the 4 antipodal pairs are -0.9996 to -1.0 (clearly the best/only near-perfect-antiparallel match for each component in the full 8x8 dot matrix), confirmed also by edge-adjacency cross-checks (rendered the shared edge between components 9 and its 3 true neighbors 10/12/13, confirming 9 touches 10,12,13 -- all DIFFERENT from its true antipode 15 -- matching expected octahedron topology where each face's 3 edge-neighbors are distinct from its 1 point-symmetric opposite). (6) Complete set {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8} confirmed with NO repeats and NO missing value -- this invariant holds. (7) ANOMALY, reported honestly rather than silently corrected: the opposite-face sums are 8, 10, 8, 10 -- NOT the standard physical-d8 convention of 9 (1-8, 2-7, 3-6, 4-5) that most commercial/physical D8 dice use. This was NOT a reading error: every face digit was independently re-verified 3+ times via different methods (including stroke-shape disambiguation explicitly checking 5-vs-6 and 7-vs-8, which have very different stroke topology -- 5 has a flat top + single bottom loop, 6 has a continuous curve + single loop, 7 is all straight lines with zero loops, 8 is two full closed loops -- these are not visually confusable even at low contrast, and brightness-boosted re-renders of the darker faces (13-16) gave identical results to the original renders). The geometric antipodal pairing is also independently solid (near-exact -1.0 dot products, cross-validated by edge topology). Conclusion: this specific CC0 PolyhedralDice D8.gltf asset was modeled/numbered without enforcing the sum-to-9 physical-dice convention; its face numbering is simply 1-8 assigned per-face without regard to opposite-sum balance. This is reported as a genuine property of the asset, not a measurement artifact -- downstream consumers (e.g. the dice engine integration) should use the face->value table above directly rather than assume a sum-9 invariant for this die.
